## Reconciled October14 status

Capability/help candidates are compiled and exercised for AUTO, RetroArch and standalone overrides at both sizes. Explicit preferences are preserved. The three French replacement descriptions have reviewed640/1280 frames in the October14 component packet; previously rejected wrapping frames remain historical.

Remaining: native emulator/save behavior and installed clean/retained qualification. The separate #581 preservation repair also needs the updated English640 long-card-path frame and native/upgrade proof. Do not equate an engine's manual-state support with configured automatic save-on-exit or frontend manager integration. Evidence: local library VM and `docs/qa-logs/2026-10-14-offline-components/README.md`.

This is a scoped readiness update under #585; all broader unproved acceptance criteria remain open. Earlier sections below retain their dated source/evidence history.

## Earlier intake and evidence history

## Owner report — October 13

> Another item I found is that on the RetroAchievements Nova, even though "Save on exit" was selected, it doesn't seem to save the session or show the EmulationStation save state manager. This might be how the emulators for GameCube and Dreamcast work, and if this is the expected behavior, then that's fine, but it is in contrast to what you have with the other retroarch cores.

Refers to the Retroid Pocket Nova. Duplicate report is one issue.

## Current behavior and investigation

The fork's es_savestates.cfg registers the frontend manager layout only for retroarch. Standalone Dolphin and Flycast have separate launchers; those launchers do not currently consume global.autosave. Dolphin's StateSaves folder exists independently of manager integration. Flycast upstream has AutoSaveState/AutoLoadState behavior, so standalone status alone is not a reason to claim the emulator cannot do it. Separate engine capability, configured launcher behavior and frontend manager support.

Already written: existing firmware offers global automatic save/load controls and preserves per-emulator/per-game preferences. Do not overwrite existing memory-card/VMU saves, save states, or enabled account settings while investigating. D-UI-057/#196 owns RetroArch auto-state correctness, which must not regress.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes: inspect exact installed configuration and exercise disposable/homebrew emulator exit/relaunch and frontend manager paths with synthetic save data. The owner report is intake, not the acceptance test. Only scoped read-only device inspection is needed to determine selected emulators; no games, saves, screenshots, input, sync or account operations are implied.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Bind the observed systems to selected emulator/core and effective automatic save/load settings; artifact/source receipt separates global preference, runtime implementation, and manager support.
- [ ] Document and verify behavior for RetroArch, standalone Dolphin and standalone Flycast using disposable VM fixtures: ordinary in-game save, manual state, exit auto-state and manager visibility are separate observations.
- [ ] If the current UI implies unsupported behavior, correct capability gating or help text with EN/FR flow references and exact-source screenshots; do not silently promise session preservation.
- [ ] Any proposed standalone integration proves exit/load/slot/path handling, clean and retained-storage behavior, existing state preservation and relevant hardcore restrictions; otherwise record the supported limitation explicitly and scope enhancement separately.

Track the inconsistency before next-candidate qualification; do not equate lack of automatic states with loss of normal game saves. Related #574 (GameCube achievement recognition, separate issue).

comments.body:
Source follow-up: accepted ES `c8dc72cf9ec00ab00d6c4a9fcdcea1746c6f1f78`, `es-app/src/SaveStateRepository.cpp` around line 211, explicitly returns false for manager support when the selected emulator is not `retroarch`. The shipped `es_savestates.cfg` likewise declares only RetroArch. Standalone Dolphin/Flycast launchers do not wire the global auto-save setting to equivalent exit/restore behavior. This explains a likely capability/expectation mismatch, not loss of ordinary game saves.

The attempted read-only Nova emulator/core-selection read timed out, so the actual selected core for the reported games is still unverified. Do not infer standalone selection merely from the platform. Next: establish selected emulator, verify per-emulator automatic-state/manual-state/manager behavior with disposable VM fixtures, and make any setting/support explanation accurately reflect that capability. A broad standalone integration is not silently promised by this diagnosis.

French catalog09afa is compiled and its three replacement save-capability descriptions now pass reviewed global/per-game frames at640×480 and1280×800 against ESbb9e. All four visual runners0, no game launch; final1280 settings byte-identical. Global640 changed only the documented legacy incremental0→2 normalization (D-UI-083; both consumer values mean off), while the selected auto-save preferences remained unchanged. The original raw-file cmp failure and follow-up source/readback evidence are retained.

The old rejected wrapping frames remain historical evidence. Canonical menu map now links the new reviewed frame index in local docs/qa-logs/2026-10-14-offline-components/. Source-staged UI qualification does not promote the production pin or qualify a new full image. The VM is complete and its media retired.
